findings.source_passage: Reach me a rose, honey, and pour me a last drop into that there crystal glass.
findings.source_locator: early party gossip paragraph, after “second cousin to the devil”
findings.why_it_matters: The flamboyant tag-line completes the satirical party voice; dropping it flattens the anecdote and amputates Fitzgerald’s period idiom.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-insert the sentence verbatim immediately after the devil–relation joke.

findings.source_passage: Clarence Endive was from East Egg, as I remember. He came only once, in white knickerbockers, and had a fight with a bum named Etty in the garden.
findings.why_it_matters: The mock-Homeric guest list relies on vivid one-off vignettes like Endive’s brawl; cutting it thins the set-piece the plan said to preserve.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full Endive sentence immediately after the Edgar Beaver line.

findings.source_passage: Of theatrical people there were Gus Waize and Horace O’Donavan and Lester Myer and George Duckweed and Francis Bull.
findings.why_it_matters: This roll-call’s comic rhythm and alliterative names are signature Nick prose; excising them dulls the satire the chapter is famous for.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-insert the theatrical-people sentence (and, if room, the ensuing New York names) to keep the catalogue’s cadence intact.

findings.source_passage: “Highballs?” asked the head waiter. … “Yes, highballs,” agreed Gatsby, and then to Mr. Wolfshiem: “It’s too hot over there.”
findings.source_locator: start of the restaurant scene with Wolfshiem
findings.why_it_matters: The clipped ‘Highballs?’ exchange is classic Fitzgerald small-talk; losing it mutes the scene’s period texture and Nick’s observational tone.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the head-waiter question and Gatsby’s ‘Yes, highballs’ reply before Wolfshiem’s Metropole nostalgia.

findings.source_passage: “You’re very polite, but I belong to another generation,” he announced solemnly. “You sit here and discuss your sports and your young ladies and your—”
findings.source_locator: Wolfshiem farewell paragraph, right before he leaves the table
findings.why_it_matters: Wolfshiem’s self-pitying generation riff is a critical character beat often cited in scholarship; cutting it erases a note of period irony.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the two missing sentences when Wolfshiem rises to leave.

summary: Five medium-level omissions drain the catalogue’s satire and Wolfshiem lunch dialogue; regenerate with the missing lines restored.
